fact: Health Minister Mustapha Ferjani said at the signing of the National Health Pact on 1 October 2026 that the shared medical record, with the national health identifier and telemedicine, was being generalised nationwide after successful pilot phases; no facility count is given.

The National Health Pact signed on 1 October 2026 by the health and communication-technologies ministers is described by the health minister as an agreement between the Ministry of Health and its partners, and he presents the shared medical record as the ministry's programme being generalised nationally.

Health Minister Mustapha Ferjani said on 29 September 2026 that the Ministry of Health aims for every Tunisian to have a unique health identifier and a digital medical record before the end of 2026, retrievable wherever the patient is treated, public or private, and hosted on a Tunisian sovereign cloud; this is a stated aim, with no coverage figure.

DH Arab, reporting the Ministry of Health's own account, says 99 healthcare facilities are at various stages of implementing electronic medical records; no denominator and no tier is given, so the number of primary clinics among them is not stated, and the figure is undated (document published 25 September 2026).

The Essaha Aziza programme's results page states that its digitalisation mission for first-line care structures developed the national computerised medical record (DMI) and monitored its deployment on pilot sites in Nabeul; no number of sites is given and the page is undated, so the record's retrieval-based published date of 3 September 2026 is used.

The national DMI for first-line care was developed under the Essaha Aziza programme, which the record's publisher line gives as a Ministry of Health and European Union programme, with training of field teams and developers delivered by the company Elligy; the page body states no amount and no domestic budget line, and is undated (published date of 3 September 2026 used).

The Ministry of Health confirmed on 21 July 2026 that the Sahetna.tn portal, through which citizens are to reach their medical records, appointments and treatments under the National Health Identifier, had completed technical validation and a cybersecurity audit reviewed by a steering committee on 10 June 2026; the portal is cleared, not yet in service.

A Ministry of Health communiqué of 21 July 2026 announced the imminent launch of the national citizen health platform Sahetna.tn, which ministry adviser Inès Ayadi said had entered its final phase of technical configuration and network deployment, giving hospital patients online access to their medical files and care history on a unified shared medical record; it was not yet in service.

La Presse reports on 21 July 2026 that the Ministry of Health's general directorate announced Sahetna.tn and the unified shared medical record as the ministry's own e-health project, with the ministry's roadmap extending the identifier and portal to private clinics and laboratories through joint technical commissions; no supplier or funder is named.

Data Landscapers' 54-country review (an AI-assisted compilation, the author's analysis) scores Tunisian rural clinics 1 and states that rural primary healthcare clinics predominantly record patient data on paper, with paper registers prevailing for patient encounters and digital effort concentrated on urban and regional hospitals; the row is undated, so the essay's publication date of 31 March 2026 is used.

fact: The World Bank's appraisal-stage PID states that the EHR (Dossier Médical Informatisé, DMI) is fully installed and used in 50 per cent of university hospitals and installed but partially used in the other 50 per cent; in regional hospitals 32 per cent are fully operational, 52 per cent installed but partially used and 16 per cent have none; no counts of hospitals are given and the figures are undated, so the PID's date of 2 April 2025 is used.

The World Bank PID states that in district hospitals and primary health centres (CSBs) EHR systems are neither installed nor used, against a stated base of over 2,000 CSBs; the statement is undated, so the PID's date of 2 April 2025 is used.

The World Bank PID, describing primary health care, states that the health system remains largely paper-based, that the Electronic Health Records pilot (DMI) faces connectivity and functionality issues, and that there is no unified registry for chronic conditions; undated, so the PID's date of 2 April 2025 is used.

GnetNews reports the Minister of Health saying, at the 10th Réalités forum on digital health, that digitisation of the medical record under the ministry's 'dossier médical unique' project had passed 95 per cent implementation; what the 95 per cent is a share of is not stated, and the capture is undated, so the record's proxy date of 2025 is used.

The Minister of Health said the next stage of the 'dossier médical unique' project would be to connect first-line health facilities to the internet and train their nurses and doctors, placing primary facilities ahead of the record rather than on it; no count of facilities is given, and the capture is undated (proxy date of 2025 used).
